newsitem.title: USA: Butler sees lower Q1, cites start-up costs.
newsitem.headline: Butler sees lower Q1, cites start-up costs.

text.p: Butler Manufacturing Co said Friday it expects a good year, but first quarter earnings will be down from a year earlier due to start-up costs in China and Brazil.

"We anticipate another good year in 1997 for Butler, but we do expect first-quarter earnings will be down from 1996, mostly because of significant current start-up costs in China and Brazil," Robert West, chairman and chief executive officer, said in a statement.
"We continue to manage the company in ways that we believe best balance short-term results with long-term growth," he said.

Butler, reporting higher 1996 results, said investments outside the United States were a major portion of its capital expenditures last year, which totaled $22 million. Spending may be slightly higher in 1997, it said.
A new metal building systems plant in Shanghai, China, was under development most of the year, and initial shipments began in December.
Equipment to produce metal building systems in Brazil was purchased in 1996 and will become operational early this year.

The Building Systems group, Butler's largest business, continued to achieve excellent results in 1996, it said. The U.S. metal buildings business had record earnings for the year. Lester wood frame buildings had lower sales and earnings but gained momentum as the year progressed after being severely impacted by bad weather in early winter.
Its Advanced Building Systems joint venture with McDonald's Corp had a start-up year that was slower than anticipated, Butler said. No details were disclosed.

Butler's European operations substantially reduced their losses compared to 1995 but were unable to reach breakeven results. Butler Real Estate made a significant contribution to corporate profitability, it said.
Butler produces pre-engineered building systems, and supplies specialty components and construction services for the nonresidential construction market.
